cards.label: A few days later — Spitalfields Market
cards.text: Archie is eating a falafel wrap and looking at his phone. He waves you over without looking up, which is either comfortable familiarity or mild rudeness. Probably both.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Alright. How'd it go with James, then?"

cards.speaker: You
cards.text: "He taught me how to make the pearls. Basic stuff, but — it worked."
Archie stops chewing. He looks at you with an expression you haven't seen on him before: genuine surprise.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "He actually showed you? How to craft?"

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Because James doesn't show people things. James does things, judges people for not knowing how to do them, and considers that a complete interaction. Either he was absolutely desperate, or —" He tilts his head. "He saw something worth the bother."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Don't let it go to your head. You're at the bottom of a very long ladder. James has been at this for thirty years and he still considers himself underappreciated, which should tell you something about the ceiling."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "That said — keep practising. Seriously. Being able to craft your own means you're not at the mercy of James's prices, which frankly are a war crime. And it's a marketable skill."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Same way the ore is. There's buyers for finished product too — people who want pearls and don't have a James. I can start lining them up. Anything you make that you don't need, bring it to me. We split it down the middle, same as the calc."
He finishes his wrap and bins the wrapper from four metres away. It goes in first time. He doesn't acknowledge this at all.
